title: Dirac's theorem: δ ≥ n/2 ⇒ Hamiltonian (formalize-only)
why_not_classical: Dirac 1952: every simple graph on n≥3 vertices with minimum degree at least n/2 is Hamiltonian. Settled undergraduate theorem. Value is a Mathlib contribution (Hamiltonian defs exist; no degree sufficient condition). Do NOT re-fund as novel. Ore is a classical strengthening — optional stretch, not v1.
recommendation: Shortlist #2 — genuinely NEW proof layer over SimpleGraph Hamiltonian API (existence of a cycle from a degree bound), not a re-warm of Friendship (windmill/common-neighbours), EKR (intersecting families), or Ramsey (cliques in colourings). Walk/Path longest-path arguments are fiddly in Lean — that is the budget risk, not the mathematics.

Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Hamiltonian.lean: defs IsHamiltonian (walk), IsHamiltonianCycle, SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian + connectivity lemmas; file ends L137; NO Dirac/Ore sufficient condition. rg -l -i dirac over Mathlib/**/*.lean hits analysis/measure Dirac, ZERO graph-theory Dirac. rg hamiltonian → Hamiltonian.lean only. statement_pin_required.convention: Fix G : SimpleGraph V, Fintype V, n = card V, 3 ≤ n, 2 * G.minDegree ≥ n. Claim: G.IsHamiltonian (Mathlib: exists a Hamiltonian cycle). Integer form of δ ≥ n/2 is 2δ ≥ n.
landmines: n ≥ 3 is essential (K2 is a counterexample to the n≥2 reading).
Mathlib IsHamiltonian singleton convention must not be used as a fake Dirac proof.
Claim is Hamiltonian CYCLE, not path; directed Dirac out of scope.
minDegree vs average; pin 2 * minDegree ≥ n.
Ore stretch only if leftover budget; not required for v1.
statement_pin_required.canonical_source: G. A. Dirac, Some theorems on abstract graphs, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 2 (1952) 69–81. Proof pin: longest-path closing (Bondy–Murty / Diestel).

feasibility_shape: Level A: n=3 + complete graphs + connectedness from δ. Level B: longest-path / cycle-closing. Walk API verbosity is the sink — cap two levels; no native_decide on 2^{n^2} graphs.
